proposals.evidence: DEDR1646 gives Tamil kuñci anything small, Malayalam kuññu/kuñci young/small, Kota kun small and Kannada gunna smallness, beside kunni young animal. Selected kuñj-/kuñc-/kunn- survey small adjectives are comparative lect extensions with ordinary adjective/neuter endings. The neighbouring child/young-animal senses are explicit in the article. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4275 gives Tamil putu/putiya new, puttaṉ new person or thing, Malayalam puttan a new thing, Kota pud and Kodagu pudiyë new. Selected puttan/putuvan/putusu/pudiyai-type survey responses include the source’s nominalized person/thing forms and ordinary adjective endings; the original new gloss is retained. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
